the two cases below; the glob case's comment restates the retired clause

summary: commitPaths commits its named paths alone, leaving whatever else the operator staged staged
acceptance: With unrelated work staged on the primary checkout, a ship tick's chore(flume) commit carries pending.json alone and the operator's staging survives untouched.
tests: commitPaths commits only its named paths when an unrelated change is staged
commitPaths refuses when its named paths hold no change and an unrelated change is staged
notes: Field-traced at 01a9a625: three operator question deletions rode into the ledger commit. `git commit --only -m <msg> -- <paths>` is the whole fix (arg order matters; -m after -- is read as a pathspec), and `run` already carries literalPathspecEnv. Two consequences to take deliberately: --only refuses mid-cherry-pick, where today's bare commit would conclude the pick; and it makes the unchanged-ledger skip (spec/pending.md, Wave auto-unblock) hold again, which a staged bystander defeats today.
